extraction.name: MATH
extraction.description: A dataset of 12,500 challenging competition mathematics problems from high school math competitions, each with a full step-by-step solution and final boxed answer, tagged by subject and difficulty.
extraction.creator: Dan Hendrycks, Collin Burns, Saurav Kadavath, Akul Arora, Steven Basart, Eric Tang, Dawn Song, Jacob Steinhardt
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Problems were collected from mathematics competitions including AMC 10, AMC 12, AIME, and more, many from the AoPS community site. The dataset was curated as competition-level math problems with step-by-step solutions, subjects, and difficulty labels.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Competition mathematics problems and solutions from contests such as AMC 10, AMC 12, AIME, including materials available via AoPS.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Final boxed answers were normalized with consistent formatting rules so equivalent answers could be matched exactly; figures were encoded in Asymptote rather than raster images.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Problems and solutions were consistently formatted in LaTeX and Asymptote, and answers were normalized using formatting rules for fractions, coefficients, variable ordering, polynomial order, parentheses, units, spaces, and equivalent numeric forms.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Each problem includes a step-by-step solution and final boxed answer. Problems are categorized into seven subjects and assigned difficulty levels 1 to 5 following AoPS.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Equivalent answer strings were analyzed and normalized so exact-match evaluation could treat multiple valid formats as the same answer.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Difficulty level and subject labels for problems; no human personal sensitive information for dataset items is described.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The authors note potential ramifications for cheating on homework or exams if models achieve strong performance, and state they do not intend the dataset to train models that help students cheat.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset is drawn from U.S. mathematics competitions and assesses the best young mathematical talent in the United States.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Current models achieve low accuracy on the dataset; scaling alone appears insufficient. The benchmark may also have implications for cheating if models improve substantially.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking and measuring mathematical problem-solving ability of machine learning models; training and fine-tuning models using problems, final answers, and step-by-step solutions; pretraining with the auxiliary AMPS corpus.

name.evidence: To measure the problem-solving ability of machine learning models, we introduce the MATH dataset, which consists of 12,500 problems from high school math competitions.

description.evidence: Many intellectual endeavors require mathematical problem solving, but this skill remains beyond the capabilities of computers. To measure this ability in machine learning models, we introduce MATH, a new dataset of 12,500 challenging competition mathematics problems. Each problem in MATH has a full step-by-step solution... In addition, MATH problems are tagged by difficulty from 1 to 5, and span seven subjects...
